outcome: Bottle- or mixed-feeding vs breast-only feeding
cohort: 45,493 pregnant women who delivered in maternity units in Trento province, North East Italy, between 2009-2018
finding: HCV positive mothers had a higher seroprevalence of hepatitis C infection and were more likely to experience intrahepatic cholestasis, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, low birth weight, elective Caesarean births, hospitalisation at birth, and bottle- or mixed-feeding compared to HCV negative mothers.
mod_finding: Elective Caesarean births were more common in HCV positive mothers.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was more common in infants born to HCV positive mothers.
